Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed, we're evaluating a Dedicated deployment for Greenline's conversational triage and patient summarization features. I attached a small sample of our production traffic (greenline_workload_sample.csv) — three days of requests exported from our proxy. High-level asks:

- 95th pct latency target for single-request inference: 300ms
- Typical model: 13B quantized (we may try 7B+variants)
- Peak concurrency observed in sample: ~420 concurrent requests; typical baseline ~60
- Response token distribution skewed: 70% short (<=32 tokens), 20% medium (33-128), 10% long (>128)

Can you provide an initial footprint estimate (GPU SKUs, node counts, warm cache strategy) and any follow-up clarifying questions? We need a rough cost/commitment ballpark for our procurement review next week.

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com

Date: 2029-05-02T10:05:00-07:00

Amir — thanks for the sample and the clear targets. I ran a quick pass on the CSV and sketched a hypothesis below (attached as fleet_estimate_template.xlsx). This is intentionally conservative in a few spots so procurement has headroom. Key assumptions and questions: 

Hypothesis (single-region, us-west):
- Model: 13B quantized (sustained perf profile we use for similar customers)
- Baseline target throughput: sustain 60 concurrent requests with p95 <= 300ms; handle spikes up to 420 with auto-burst/fallback
- Warm-cache: prefix and KV caching expected to yield ~25% token-cost reduction for repeat prompts; we recommend a warm pool of 20% of fleet for hot-session affinity
- GPU SKU: A2-equivalent (32GB) for 13B-quantized; 1 GPU supports ~18 sustained concurrent short requests (<=32 tokens) at p95 250-300ms in our internal profile
- Initial node count estimate: 24 GPUs (4 nodes x 6 GPUs) to cover baseline with buffer; burst target uses autoscale to 36 GPUs for sustained peaks.
- Autoscaling policy suggestion: 60s window, CPU+GPU utilization + median queue depth trigger; add preferred fallback to 7B variant for best-effort latency preservation

Clarifying questions (so we can tighten the estimate):
1) What % of your requests include function/tool calls or structured outputs (these increase CPU work and response time)?
2) Do you require strict per-request token accounting for billing / audit?
3) Are there predictable daily or weekly traffic tides (e.g., Monday morning bulk intake) we should know about?
4) Any hard constraints on cold-starts or acceptable warm-up times for new sessions?

Next steps: Marissa (cc'd) will prepare a commit/price ballpark once we confirm the answers above and we can align on a SLA+SLO template. Dev, can you confirm whether the A2-equivalent mapping is OK or if you'd prefer a different GPU baseline?

Attachments: fleet_estimate_template.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

Cheers,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
From: Amir Bashir <amir.b@greenlinehealth.com>

Thanks, Evelyn — this is exactly the kind of hatchet estimate we need. Quick answers inline: 

On May 2, 2029, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com> wrote:
> 1) What % of your requests include function/tool calls or structured outputs?
We estimate ~8% include external tool calls (EHR lookups) and ~12% request structured JSON.

> 2) Do you require strict per-request token accounting for billing / audit?
Yes — procurement wants token-level logs retained for 90 days (audit).

> 3) Are there predictable daily or weekly traffic tides?
Yes — heavy volume Mon/Tue 07:00-13:00 PT and smaller evening spike 18:00-20:00 PT. Weekends ~30% of weekday baseline.

> 4) Any hard constraints on cold-starts or acceptable warm-up times?
We need user-facing latency within 500ms for 95% of requests; cold-starts are acceptable up to 2s but we'd prefer <1s when possible.

Also, the long responses (>128 tokens) correlate with patient summarization flows and are often batched at peak times. I've attached a cleaner export with 95th/99th token percentiles for the three-day window.

Attachments: greenline_workload_sample_v2.csv (text/csv, 210KB)

Can you update the hypothesis with the tooling overhead and the retention requirement? Procurement is trying to model a 12-month committed capacity and would like a ballpark monthly cost.

—Amir

Team — forwarding Greenline's clarifications. I updated the worksheet to include: tooling overhead (+10% CPU for structured outputs and external calls), token-log retention lift (adds ~8% storage & egress baseline), and adjusted burst headroom for Monday tides. High-level ask: can we confirm the A2-equivalent (32GB) mapping and whether the warm-pool approach (20% hot nodes) is realistic for their p95 SLA given the cold-start tolerance?

Specific asks:
- Marissa: generate a 12-month committed price band for 24/36/48 GPU commitments (include potential discount tiers and explicit overage pricing). Use DEAL-2029-0037 hubspot link.
- Dev: validate the 1 GPU ~18 sustained short-request concurrency assumption for our quantized 13B image on A2-equivalents; if your bench shows >=22, that materially changes node counts. Please also note KV cache hit-rate sensitivity (we need a conservative 15-25% range).
- Jordan: propose an autoscale policy (metric triggers + cooldowns) that meets Amir's 60s window and preserves session affinity for warm-pool percentage. Also include a fallback routing plan to a 7B variant during sustained overloads.

I left Amir on the thread to keep them in the loop; we'll synthesize and send the final ballpark to procurement by EOD Friday.
